target.purpose: Spend a finite annotation budget preferentially on items with the greatest uncertainty or prior disagreement while preserving deterministic global and per-item bounds.
target.central_bottleneck: Uniform k-label policies waste scarce annotation capacity on easy items and make underfunded decisions depend on incidental input ordering instead of explicit need.
success: All normalized need inputs are finite and within [0,1].
Duplicate or empty item identities refuse before allocation.
Allocation never exceeds the global label budget or per-item ceiling.
Underfunded baselines and tied scores are deterministic.
Extra agreement rounds are reserved for materially uncertain or disputed items.
Python and Go surfaces preserve the same allocation invariants.

invariants: deterministic score ordering and tie breaking
global annotation budget is never exceeded
per-item annotation ceiling is never exceeded
no external labeling side effect occurs

donor_plan.basis: The repository already implements the allocation mechanism; sibling Scale-lens repositories own different quality/integrity concerns.

nonclaims: not a production Scale AI allocation service
no external labeling jobs are executed
no label correctness or annotator-quality conclusion is produced
no exercised integration with the collusion or eval-poison sibling repositories
